newsitem.title: CHINA: China rules out early talks with Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: China rules out early talks with Taiwan.

text.p: A top Chinese official responsible for contacts with Taiwan has ruled out any early resumption of talks with the island on reunification, the China Daily said on Tuesday.

Tang Shubei, vice-chairman of the Association for Relations across the Taiwan Strait (ARATS), said there was no possibility of talks until Taiwan's leader, President Lee Teng-hui, abandoned "splittist" activities aimed at independence for the island that Beijing regards as a renegade province.
Talks between the two sides were broken off after President Lee made a landmark private visit to the United States in mid-1995, enraging Beijing which wants to isolate the island diplomatically.
"In the long term the mainland and Taiwan should sit down at the negotiating table to discuss cross-straits issues under the 'one-China' policy," Tang was quoted as saying in the China Daily.
But he said the atmosphere for talks would not improve in the short term unless Lee halted his "splittist" activities.
"We have the patience to handle the issue of the peaceful reunification of the motherland," Tang said.
